inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 129.4M common shares at 30-Jun-2026 ($1 par common stock line, Q2-26 balance sheet) + ~0.5M dilutive awards (Q2-26 diluted 130.3M vs basic 129.8M weighted). Held FLAT because SBC (incl. withholding taxes) is fully expensed in the flows; VMC is an active repurchaser ($438M FY25, $400M H1-26) so the flat count is funded, not a convention. Q3-26 buybacks not yet reported.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 cash-flow SBC add-back $63.1M + shares withheld for taxes on equity awards $34.0M (financing activities) = $97.1M; VMC publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. H1-26: $24.7M + $38.3M.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD build: 10y UST ~4.3%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.95 -> cost of equity ~9.1%. Debt $4.4B at ~5.0% pre-tax (~3.9% after tax) against ~$31.6B market cap -> ~12% debt weight. WACC 8.5%, identical across scenarios: cyclicality (housing, IIJA reauthorisation) is charged in the bear/bull flows, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842 operating leases are already expensed inside cost of sales, so adjusted EBITDA is post-lease (treatment B by construction). Operating lease liabilities (~$0.6B incl. current) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases are immaterial ($4.9M H1-26 payments).
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest is immaterial ($1.4M H1-26 distributions); ignored.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing: US operating company, cyclical construction materials) with the cyclical adaptations (risk charged once in the flows, lower terminal cap than a compounder). Not a REIT/bank/holdco. FY0 = FY2025 ($7,941.1M revenue, CSV EBITDA $2,368.1M). Anchors refreshed to the Q2-26 10-Q/earnings release (8-K ex99.1, 29-Jul-2026), which the Metrics CSV does not yet carry (it ends at Q1-26): total debt $4,364.3M, cash+restricted cash $288.7M, company-defined net debt $4,075.6M. GUIDANCE: FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA $2.4-2.6B reaffirmed (midpoint $2.5B; D&A ~$700M; interest ~$215M). VMC's Adjusted EBITDA does NOT add back SBC, so ebitda_margin_path here is (Adj EBITDA + SBC)/revenue to avoid charging SBC twice: FY26 ~ ($2,500 + ~$60)/~$8,100 = 31.6%. FY26 revenue growth is only ~2% because the Houston asphalt/construction business (sold Q4-25) and California ready-mix (sold Jun-26, $572M H1 divestiture proceeds) drop out of H2; H1-26 reported revenue was +4.7%. Growth paths are ORGANIC (price + volume); bolt-on M&A is not modelled, neither its cash cost nor its revenue. Working capital: adjusted NWC ~$945M on ~$8.1B revenue (~11.7%), so wc_capture is NEGATIVE (-12% of revenue increase). Interest income not stripped: VMC carries net debt. Buybacks recorded but value-neutral (flat count). Pension and asset-retirement obligations not added to the bridge (in the flows as accretion / contributions). Analysis JSON was not present at build time; scenario axes drawn from the filings and the Q2-26 release.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (7.2%) diverges >30% from EPS 3yr CAGR (23.5%) and revenue 3yr CAGR (2.8%). Revenue 5yr (10.3%) is inflated by the US Concrete (2021) acquisition; the 3yr EPS/FCF CAGRs start from a depressed FY2022 base (cost inflation). The forward base path uses ~5-6% organic growth (mid-single-digit aggregates pricing + ~0-1% volume), below the selected equity CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding taxes (no interest income strip; net debt). Owner-FCF CAGRs (29.7% 3yr, 9.7% 5yr) sit slightly above reported (28.5%, 9.9% -> 3yr owner above because FY22 base is small); SBC is ~1% of revenue so the adjustment is minor. FY2025 owner FCF $1,038.2M vs reported $1,135.3M.

base.narrative: FY26 at guidance midpoint ($2.5B adj EBITDA), then mid-single-digit aggregates pricing plus modest volume; cash gross profit per ton keeps compounding as the mix shifts to pure-play aggregates.

bull.narrative: Top of guidance, then a highway reauthorisation at or above IIJA levels, data-centre/manufacturing/LNG megaprojects and a residential recovery lift volumes 2-3%/yr on top of 5-6% pricing.

bear.narrative: A 2027-28 construction downturn: IIJA lapses into short-term extensions, residential stays weak and private non-res megaprojects pause; volumes fall high-single-digits while price still rises ~3%, unit-cost deleverage and diesel compress margins ~3pp before a slow recovery.

scenario_narratives.base: Vulcan executes its pure-play aggregates strategy: FY2026 lands at the $2.5B adjusted-EBITDA midpoint despite energy inflation and wet Q2 weather, then freight-adjusted pricing compounds at ~4-5% (Q2-26: +5% mix-adjusted) with 0-2% volume growth supported by public construction and large projects. Cash gross profit per ton keeps rising (>$12 in Q2-26) and the exit from Houston asphalt and California ready-mix lifts the group margin, taking (EBITDA+SBC)/revenue from ~31.6% to ~34.5% by 2031. Capex runs slightly above D&A; 15-20% of revenue converts to unlevered owner FCF. Organic only - bolt-on acquisitions (e.g. the Brannan quarry and DFW rail yard) are treated as value-neutral at the price paid.
scenario_narratives.bull: The aggregates pricing cycle stays unusually strong: a federal surface-transportation reauthorisation at or above IIJA funding, a wave of data-centre, semiconductor, LNG and manufacturing megaprojects in VMC's Sun Belt footprint, and a residential recovery as mortgage rates ease together lift volumes 2-3%/yr on top of 5-6% price. Operating leverage on a fixed quarry cost base and continued SAG discipline (6.9% of revenue TTM) push the margin to ~37%. Terminal growth 3.5% reflects irreplaceable, permitted reserves near growing metros.
scenario_narratives.bear: IIJA expires on 30-Sep-2026 and is followed by a run of short-term extensions instead of a full reauthorisation, state DOT lettings slow, residential stays depressed and private non-residential megaprojects are deferred. Shipments fall high-single-digits across 2027-28 (as in 2008-10, though far less severe) while pricing still rises ~3%; fixed-cost deleverage plus diesel and liquid-asphalt inflation compress margins ~3pp before a slow recovery to ~31%. Capex is cut to defend cash. Terminal growth 2.5% and a 15x cap reflect a lower-multiple cyclical rerating.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% house default): IIJA authorisation lapses 30-Sep-2026 with no successor bill yet, and residential/private non-res demand is soft, so a cyclical volume downturn is a live near-term path. Base 50%: guidance was reaffirmed in July and pricing remains positive. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs a full-funding highway bill, sustained megaproject activity and a housing recovery together - several independent things.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Vulcan is a high-quality, locally-monopolistic aggregates franchise whose value lies in permitted reserves and pricing power, but it remains a construction cyclical. The house view charges SBC and equity-award withholding taxes in full, models organic growth only, charges the cycle once through a 25%-weighted downturn scenario rather than a WACC premium, and caps the terminal at 15-20x FCF. The market currently pays ~27x unlevered owner FCF, which this model only supports in the bull case. The price sits above even the street (SBC-as-non-cash) value in the base case, so band_position exceeds 100%: the gap to the price is a growth/multiple question, not an SBC-accounting one.
key_risks_to_valuation: Federal highway funding: IIJA expires 30-Sep-2026; reauthorisation size and timing drive public volumes (the largest end market)
Residential and private non-residential construction cyclicality (rates, megaproject timing)
Energy (diesel, liquid asphalt) cost inflation compressing unit margins, as seen in Q2-26 (+7% unit cash cost)
Weather volatility in Texas and the Southeast shifting volumes between periods
M&A: growth via acquisitions is not modelled; overpaying would destroy value the model does not show
Terminal multiple: 55-66% of enterprise value sits in the terminal (base 61%); each 1pp of terminal growth moves the base value materially
